D.t: Rob Sand leads by 10.8 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 148,395 votes; a one point swing is about 6,864 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +3.8 and D +18.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is D +6.6. Your best recent poll is Cook Political Report/GS Strategy Group and New River Strategies at D +11.0; your worst is On Point Polling at D +4.7. 13 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Polk, a projected net 83,523 votes; Johnson, a projected net 43,860 votes; Linn, a projected net 36,392 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Pottawattamie, D +9.2, 2.5% of the vote; Woodbury, R +2.2, 2.5% of the vote; Warren, D +8.7, 1.9% of the vote; Clinton, D +6.4, 1.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Rob Sand runs furthest behind in Sioux, Marion, Dallas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.50 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 71% of voters, 52 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.57 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 60 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Rob Sand: Immigration voters 26 to 74, Small counties 43 to 55, Voters who can afford daily costs 49 to 51. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Democrats cast 51% of the 207,774 ballots in Iowa so far, against 32% for the other party. That is 4.7 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 1.3 points away from Rob Sand. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
